sentences.text: 1 has put in appearance on behalf of respondent no. 2 - Project Director, National Highways Authority of India.

2. This is a wholly cryptic petition filed by the petitioner seeking for the reliefs as under :-
"21(B) This Hon'ble Court may be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus or writ in the nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or direction calling upon the respondents to pay the compensation of petitioner's non agriculture commercial land bearing old block no. 48 and NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5756/2020 ORDER DATED: 06/01/2025 undefined new survey no. 1545 and 1543 admeasuring 290 sq.meter situated at sim of village Aslali, Taluka, Dascroi, District Ahmedabad as it is granted to other claimants with interest at 18%.
(C) This Hon'ble Court may be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus or writ in the nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or direction calling upon the respondents to measure the petitioner's land being old block no. 48 and new survey no. 1543 on the spot and be pleased to direct respondents to pay compensation of the petitioner's land acquired for four lane road situated at Aslali,
Taluka Dascroi, District Ahmedabad

ALTERNATIVELY Be pleased to issue appropriate writ, order or direction to return the part of the land admeasuring 29 sq.mtr., of the petitioner wherein possession is taken over without affording any compensation of petitioner's old block no. 48 survey no. 1543, situated at village Aslali, Taluka Dascroi, District Ahmedabad in the interest of justice."
3. We may note, at the outset, that the present petitioner has filed a Special Civil Application No.
16983 of 2019, which has been dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 04.10.2019 on the request of the learned counsel for the petitioner, noticing the statement of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the relevant material could not be annexed with the writ petition and the relevant facts could not be incorporated.

The present petition has been filed on 03.03.2020 stating that the petitioner is the owner and occupier of the land bearing Old block/survey no. 48 (new block/survey no. 1543) situated at Village Aslali, Taluka Daskroi, District - Ahmedabad NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5756/2020 ORDER DATED: 06/01/2025 undefined which is on National Highway No. 8 and is a non-agricultural land (NA).
It is stated that the respondent no. 2, namely the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) had made a proposal to acquire the land of Village Aslali for six lane road.
A notification dated 15.06.2012 under Section 3A of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1956") has been published.

It is stated that in the said notification the petitioners block/survey no. 48 was not included and, therefore there was no reason for the petitioner to file any objection within 21 days of the publication of the notification.

It is further stated that Section 3D notification was published in the Official Gazette and an award was declared under Section 3G under the Act, 1956 on 30.03.2013.
3.1.
As per the statement made in paragraph '3.1' of the writ petition, a copy of the notification under Section 3A dated 23.10.2012 is appended a Annexure-'A'.

However, a perusal of the document appended on page '21' of the paper book indicates that it is a notification under Section 3D(1) of the Nam Group Aslal Through Co-Owner Anand ... vs Competent Authority And 2Nd Special ... on 6 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54658008/
2 Act, 1956 and declaration by the Central Government that the land specified in the schedule annexed thereto shall vest absolutely in the Central Government free from all encumbrances.

sentences.text: Simultaneously, a public notice dated 07.01.2013 under Section 3G (3) of the Act, 1956 for inviting claims NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5756/2020 ORDER DATED: 06/01/2025 undefined from all the persons interested in the land to be acquired in view of Section 3A notification dated 15.06.2012 and Section 3D notification dated 23.10.2012.

The name of the Village Aslali, Taluka Daskroi,
District - Ahmedabad is included in the said notification.

3.2. Placing the description of the details of the plots notified for acquisition as per the schedule attached to the notification dated 23.10.2012, it is sought to be argued by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the land belonging to the petitioner of old block/survey no. 48 (new block/survey no. 1543) situated at Village Aslali, Taluka Daskroi, District - Ahmedabad had not been included in the acquisition notifications which were published for the purposes of widening/six laning, maintenance, management and operation of N.H. 8 on the stretch of land from Kms 6/400 to Km 21/900 (Ahmedabad-Vadodara Section) in District Ahmedabad, State of Gujarat.

3.3. The petitioner also seeks to place a copy of form no. 7/12 of the land bearing block/survey no.
48 to assert that the land in question was non-agricultural land and was used for commercial purposes as the petitioner was doing the business on the said land.

It is then stated that in paragraph '3.3.' of the writ petition that the possession of the petitioner's land admeasuring 290 sq.meter was resumed by NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5756/2020 ORDER DATED: 06/01/2025 undefined the respondent authority without adopting due process of law and without making payment of compensation to the petitioner.

Though the date of dispossession of the petitioner has not been indicated in the said paragraph, however, it is submitted that the petitioner had written a letter to the respondent no. 1, namely the competent authority/Special Land Acquisition Officer,
NHAI on 24.03.2014 with the request to offer compensation for the acquired area admeasuring 294 sq.mtr.
3.4.

Simultaneously, the petitioner also wrote letter to the District Inspector of Land Records (DILR) dated 11.01.2019 for getting measurement of the land in question to determine as to how much area of the land in question had been taken by the NHAI without adopting due process of law.

The reference to the DILR report and measurement sheet appended at Annexure-'C' (Colly.) has been made to submit that the DILR report indicates that approximately 435 sq.mtr., of land of Old block/Survey no. 48 (new block/survey no. 1539) was acquired for construction of the road.
Similarly, the land of block/survey no. 1545 about 67 sq.mtr. was acquired for the road.

However,
there is no averment in the said paragraph about acquisition of Old block/survey no. 48 (new block/survey no. 1543), which according to the petitioner belongs to him as per the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5756/2020 ORDER DATED: 06/01/2025 undefined statement made in paragraph '3.1.' of the writ petition.
There is thus, no clarification as to the plot numbers assigned to Old block/survey no. 48 during the promulgation or if there are other co-owners of the said land.

4. Be that as it may, the repeated assertions made in the writ petition is that the petitioners have not received any compensation for his old block/survey no. 48 admeasuring 484 sq.mtrs., out of which 290 sq.mtr. was acquired for the purpose of the road.
As noted above, the total area of Old block/survey no. 48 has not been indicated in the writ petition.
The prayer in the writ petition is to Nam Group Aslal Through Co-Owner Anand ... vs Competent Authority And 2Nd Special ...

3 issue a direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the respondent to pay compensation of the petitioner's non-agricultural commercial Old block/survey no. 48 and new block/survey nos.
1545 and 1543 admeasuring 290 sq.mtr., situated at the sim of Village Aslali, Taluka Daskroi,
District Ahmedabad or in the alternative to return the part of the land admeasuring 290 sq.mtr., to the petitioner on which the possession has been taken over without providing compensation to him.

4.1. Noticing the above, we may further record that though there is an averment in paragraph '3.3.'
of the writ petition about the entry of Form- 7/12 and the order by the competent authority, but only a NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5756/2020 ORDER DATED: 06/01/2025 undefined letter dated 24.03.2014 sent by the petitioner to the competent authority, NHAI has been appended with the writ petition as Annexure-'B'.
The petitioner has not furnished Form 7/12 extract to establish as to which of part of the land bearing Old block/survey no. 48 came in the share of the petitioner.

A perusal of Annexure-'C' (Collectively), containing the report and measurement sheet appended at page '34' of the paper book indicates that there is a reference of two plots, namely block/survey no.1539 (old block/survey no. 46 paiki) and block/survey nos. 1545 (old block/survey no. 49 paiki).
However, there is no reference of old block/survey no. 48 or new block/survey no. 1543 which belongs to the petitioner as per the statement made in paragraph '3'1' of the writ petition.

5. From the above noted facts, it is more than evident that the petitioner has not come with correct and complete facts pertaining to his claim of acquisition of his land bearing old block/survey no. 48 (new block/survey no. 1543) situated at Village Aslali, Taluka Daskroi, District - Ahmedabad for the purposes of widening/six laning of the National Highway (N.H. 8) as a result of acquisition vide notification under Section 3D dated 23.10.2012.

It is, thus, not possible for us to issue any positive mandamus so as to draw any NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5756/2020 ORDER DATED:
06/01/2025 undefined analogy from the measurement sheet which is appended at Annexure-'C' to the writ petition containing description of two different lands carved out of old block/survey no. 49 paiki.
6. For the aforesaid, the present petition stands dismissed.

However, liberty rests with the petitioner to approach the Collector, Ahmedabad by writing a representation raising a dispute about the utilization of his land, namely old block/survey no. 48 (new block/survey no. 1543) situated at Village Aslali, Taluka Daskroi, District - Ahmedabad in the matter of widening/six laning of National Highway (N.H.8), for which acquisition process was completed with the notification issued under Section 3D dated 23.10.2012 and the award dated 30.03.2013 passed under Section 3G of the Act, 1956.
The petitioner may file an application along with the copy of this order.
On the presentation of the said application, it would be open to the Collector, Ahmedabad to make inquiry at his own ends by issuing necessary directions to the revenue authorities.
